definition: Whether a reported result can be obtained again, and across 7 sources a property the archive treats as scarce enough to be worth measuring. Its instances divide by what fails to reproduce. Method-level: an independent reproduction matches a published grid to two decimal places and then finds the advantage vanishing on every new domain, with no per-item difference reaching significance across four of them. Instrument-level: if two runs on the same activations give different dictionaries, a claim about a feature is a claim about a run -- which is the sparse-autoencoder identifiability problem stated as a reproducibility one. Protocol-level: measured performance depends on template, decoder, controller, reducer, verifier, stopping rule and numerical settings, so accuracy reported without the inference protocol is not reproducible in principle; one source prescribes declaring budget, temperature, evidence map, stopping and extraction rules before outcomes are inspected. Numerical-level: one source studies sources of nondeterminism in inference itself. The archive's practice, where sources model it well, is byte-identical prompts verified by hash, fixed seeds, and pre-registration of thresholds before the confirmatory analysis.

evidence.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
evidence.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

evidence.note: Treats test-time scaling as routing rather than budgeting -- cheap evidence decides whether a decision is already settled, and expensive verification is spent only on candidates that can still change the answer -- and evaluates every baseline by replaying it over the same stored candidate pool so that only the allocation decision differs.
evidence.title: CoBa: Cost-Effective Test-Time Scaling via Compute-Balanced Routing

evidence.note: Independently reproduces two published reliability methods and stress-tests them across models and domains their authors never tried, finding one reproduces exactly but loses significance everywhere new, and the other rests on a decodable logic direction that a same-norm random direction matches exactly under steering.
evidence.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing

evidence.note: An open library giving vision-language models the mechanistic-interpretability tooling that text-only models already have: activation patching, attention analysis and meta-functions behind one interface.
evidence.title: Spectra: A Mechanistic Interpretability Library for Vision-Language Models

evidence.note: A position paper arguing mechanistic interpretability cannot be used in safety-critical settings until its findings are auditable, and proposing continuous collaborative reviewing plus source-based claim tracking.
evidence.title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing

evidence.note: Argues run-to-run feature consistency should be a standard SAE evaluation axis alongside reconstruction and sparsity, and gives a metric showing high consistency is achievable.
evidence.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in Sparse Autoencoders

evidence.note: Shows that greedy decoding is not deterministic across hardware: changing GPU type, GPU count or evaluation batch size shifts a reasoning model's AIME'24 accuracy by up to 9 percentage points and its response length by 9,000 tokens under BF16, because floating-point addition is non-associative.
evidence.title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference

name: reproducibility
